answer: An agent market requires every identity to lock a refundable $100 bond for 30 days before receiving one trading slot per minute. An attacker can name bots after an oasis, a marble quarry, or a mesa, but each extra identity still needs its own bond; splitting one funded account creates no extra slots. Running 10,000 sybils therefore ties up $1 million for a month, imposing a capital cost rather than trusting names or account age.
